headline: Crypto broke higher into the weekend with Bitcoin up 6.1 percent to 81,087 dollars and Solana up 11.3 percent, while the US 10 year Treasury yield ended the week back near 5 percent at 4.998 and India's Nifty posted a sixth straight weekly loss, its longest losing run in six years.

summary.us: The S&P 500 edged up 0.17 percent to 7,650.50 and the Nasdaq Composite added 0.39 percent to 26,522.54 on Friday, while the Dow slipped 0.18 percent to 51,682.64 and closed the week 1.69 percent lower, in a quadruple witching session two days after the Federal Reserve raised rates a quarter point to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first hike since 2023. The 10 year Treasury yield finished at 4.998 percent after touching a 19 year high above 5.04 percent earlier in the week, and JPMorgan economists now look for another hike in December and have raised their long run policy rate estimate to 3.25 percent.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 rose 0.33 percent to 23,346.40 and Bank Nifty gained 0.54 percent to 56,358.70 on Friday, but both benchmarks closed a sixth straight losing week, the longest run in six years, weighed down by crude above 100 dollars and tighter global policy. TCS fell 3.88 percent as the Tata Sons and Tata Trusts dispute over N Chandrasekaran's term and a possible holding company listing deepened, FII and DII were both modest net buyers in the cash segment at 599.50 crore and 1,019.70 crore rupees, and the rupee firmed 0.28 percent to 95.863 while RBI data showed reserves down 4.92 billion dollars to 780.78 billion dollars in the week to 11 September.
summary.global: The Bank of Japan lifted its policy rate to a 31 year high of 1.25 percent in a 7 to 2 vote and the yen still weakened past 156 per dollar, lifting the Nikkei 1.38 percent to 65,018.95, while the KOSPI jumped 2.66 percent on Samsung and SK Hynix as 64 gigabyte DDR5 server module contract prices reached 1,500 dollars, about 5.5 times the level of a year ago. European indices fell on quadruple witching, with the DAX down 1.60 percent and the FTSE 100 down 1.45 percent, and crude eased, with CNBC putting the WTI settlement at 100.30 dollars and Brent at 103.87 dollars; the larger one day drop shown on this dashboard reflects the Yahoo futures series rolling to a later contract rather than the move in the settlement.

calendar.what: The NSE and Sonaselection India IPOs close in India. Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee speaks, opening a heavy week of Fed speakers flagged by Kitco after the 16 September rate hike.
Varmora Granito IPO opens in India at a band of 140 to 148 rupees. Weekly Nifty options expiry, which now falls on Tuesday. NSE IPO allotment expected.

S&P Global flash US manufacturing and services PMIs for September at 09:45 US Eastern. Elevate Campuses and ArMee Infotech IPOs open in India. Bamboo Insurance and Amaero are on the IPOScoop calendar to price in the US.
Costco and Nike report after the US close. A-One Steels India IPO opens at a band of 385 to 405 rupees and Varmora Granito closes.
Elevate Campuses and ArMee Infotech IPOs close in India.
Nifty and Bank Nifty September monthly futures and options expiry, the last Tuesday of the month.
US personal income and outlays with the PCE price index, per the BEA release schedule. Micron reports. Elevate Campuses and ArMee Infotech list.
RBI monetary policy committee meets 5 to 7 October, with the repo rate at 5.25 percent after the August review.

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to central banks. The Federal Reserve raised rates a quarter point on 16 September to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first hike since 2023, and the Bank of Japan followed on 18 September with a split 7 to 2 vote that lifted its policy rate to a 31 year high of 1.25 percent, yet the yen weakened past 156 per dollar because two board members dissented and Governor Ueda made no commitment to further moves. US equities finished mixed as the 10 year Treasury yield came back to about 5 percent after touching a 19 year high above 5.04 percent ahead of the Fed, with the Dow down 1.69 percent on the week while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.72 percent. India was the weak spot, where the Nifty and Sensex logged a sixth consecutive weekly decline, the longest losing run in six years, under crude above 100 dollars, tighter global policy and a deepening Tata Sons governance dispute. Metals held their ground, with copper up about 2 percent on the week as the Yangshan import premium climbed 72 percent in September to a near four year high and silver adding 3.46 percent, while crypto turned sharply higher into the weekend on post Fed relief and rotation into altcoins. Next week brings S&P Global flash PMIs on 23 September, a heavy run of Fed speakers, Costco and Nike earnings on 24 September, and in India the Varmora Granito, Elevate Campuses, ArMee Infotech and A-One Steels offers alongside the close of the NSE IPO on 21 September.
